title: 2.3 Natural and Human Induced Climate Change
description: Milankovitch cycles, solar output, volcanic aerosols, land use change and greenhouse gas emissions. Hard level.

questions.question: Why do natural aerosols from wildfires and dust storms cool the surface?
options: They increase the greenhouse effect
They prevent sunlight from reaching the ground
Beneath an ocean rather than along a coastline
They absorb all infrared radiation
questions.correctAnswer: They prevent sunlight from reaching the ground

questions.question: How do human activities change climate through atmospheric composition?
options: It may shrink to less than 10 percent of the Arctic Ocean
They have moved relative to each other over geologic time
It releases additional carbon dioxide into the atmosphere
By adding greenhouse gases and aerosols to the atmosphere
questions.correctAnswer: By adding greenhouse gases and aerosols to the atmosphere

questions.question: What does extremely likely mean in the 2013 IPCC report?
options: A statement with no probability
A warm year disproves climate change
A probability of at least 95 percent
A probability of exactly 50 percent
questions.correctAnswer: A probability of at least 95 percent

questions.question: What did the 2013 Fifth Assessment Report conclude?
options: Sudden ground shaking caused by rock masses changing position below the surface
Human influence is the dominant cause of warming since the mid-twentieth century
Changes systems undergo in response to climate regardless of any policy or plan
Mitigation reduces future warming while adaptation reduces current and near-term impacts
questions.correctAnswer: Human influence is the dominant cause of warming since the mid-twentieth century

questions.question: Why can city nights be warmer than nearby rural nights?
options: It explains rock ages and fossil distribution patterns
Urban surfaces and haze alter the local energy balance
Implementation of the Marrakesh Accords became central
They absorb more solar energy than snow-covered tundra
questions.correctAnswer: Urban surfaces and haze alter the local energy balance

questions.question: How does albedo change contribute to warming after deforestation?
options: It eases impacts but does not limit the underlying climate change
A vent is a crack that builds a plateau; a fissure builds a cone
Altered reflectivity changes the amount of solar energy absorbed
Orbital variations help initiate glacial and interglacial periods
questions.correctAnswer: Altered reflectivity changes the amount of solar energy absorbed

questions.question: How long does carbon dioxide remain in the atmosphere according to the text?
options: About 10 years
Less than one year
Over 100 years
About 1,000,000 years

questions.question: Why are natural and human causes distinguished by mechanism?
options: Mitigation reduces future warming while adaptation reduces current and near-term impacts
Ethiopia can adopt modern efficient technologies directly instead of high-emission pathways
Natural causes can work through all three external mechanisms while humans mainly use two
A vent is a pipe-like opening that builds a cone; a fissure is a narrow crack that builds a plateau
questions.correctAnswer: Natural causes can work through all three external mechanisms while humans mainly use two

questions.question: What is the link between Milankovitch cycles and ice ages?
options: Warmer air holds more snow inland while coastal melting increases
Dark forests absorb more sunlight than snow, accelerating warming
An increase in desert conditions from overgrazing and cultivation
Orbital variations help initiate glacial and interglacial periods
questions.correctAnswer: Orbital variations help initiate glacial and interglacial periods

questions.question: Which gas is released mainly by burning coal, oil and natural gas?
options: Nitrous oxide from forests
Carbon dioxide
Methane from wetlands
Water vapor from oceans
